Contact

Bug reports, feature requests, questions

Every message lands in the author's inbox. For a bug, the most useful report says what you did, what you expected, what happened instead, and which version you are on (Preferences shows it). If a log line matters, paste it; the app's own Send feedback dialog can attach a scrubbed log slice for you.

Best for bugs: it stays public, others can add to it, and you can follow the fix. Open an issue.

From inside the app

Send feedback in the nav drawer fills in your version and can attach a log slice you review first.

This form

Anything else, or if you would rather not use GitHub. Replies come from Zeratfule@gmail.com.

pages.guides:
EQ ZERA
What it does Guides Contact What's new GitHub

Guides

Setting up and customising EQ Zera

Short how-tos for the things people ask about most. Each one assumes EQ Zera is installed; if it is not, start here.

First run Overlays over the game Sound alerts and rules Quest tracker Loot, upgrades and farming Sharing your setup Updates and versions Troubleshooting

First run

  1. In EverQuest Legends type /log on. The game starts writing a plain-text log for the character you are on. It keeps logging across sessions until you turn it off.
  2. Start EQ Zera. It looks for the log folder in the default install location, usually C:\Users\Public\Daybreak Game Company\Installed Games\EverQuest Legends\Logs. If your game lives elsewhere, point it at the folder in Preferences.
  3. Each log file is one character. Switch characters in the app and it re-reads that character's log; every view is per character.
  4. Fight something. The Combat tab fills in with the fight, and the Overview shows your last session.

A new install reads the whole existing log once, so a large log from months of play takes a moment the first time. After that it follows the file live.

Overlays over the game

Overlays are small always-on-top windows: a damage or healing meter for the current fight or the whole zone, a farm meter with kills, XP, drops and coin per hour, buff timers, and the celebration overlay where quest, loot and update cards appear.

  1. Run the game in windowed or borderless windowed mode. Exclusive fullscreen cannot be overlaid by any program.
  2. Open Preferences → Overlays and switch on the ones you want.
  3. Drag an overlay where you want it. Lock it and it becomes click-through, so it never steals a click from the game.
  4. Quest item pop-ups have their own switch in the same pane, with a filter for quests your classes can take and a choice of how long the same item waits before it pops again.

Sound alerts and rules

An alert plays a sound when something happens in the log: a charm break, a buff fading, a raid target dying, a wished item dropping, or any line you write a rule for.

  1. Open Alerts. The built-in alerts are listed with their sounds; switch them on or off and pick a sound for each.
  2. To alert on your own text, add a rule with the phrase the log line contains. Test it by making the line happen in game.
  3. Sounds come from packs. Alerts → Sound packs… lists the community packs you can install from inside the app. To add your own, drop a folder with your .wav, .mp3 or .ogg files and a small manifest.json naming them into %AppData%\everquest-companion\soundpacks\your-pack\; it shows up in every sound picker.
  4. Any alert, or all of them at once, copies to a short paste-safe string. Paste it in guild chat or Discord; whoever pastes it back in gets a preview before anything is added. Imports only ever add, never overwrite.

Quest tracker

  1. Open the Quests tab and find the quest. Quest pages come from the EQ Legends wiki, with steps built from its walkthrough.
  2. Press Track. The quest's steps become a checklist.
  3. Play. Looting a required item lights its step, hailing the quest NPC ticks the hail step, and turning in the items ticks the hand-in steps. Turning in every required item completes the quest with a card on the celebration overlay and your quest-complete alert.
  4. Loot an item any quest needs or hands out and a pop-up names the quest, its giver and start zone, with the step that needs the item lit. Click it to open the quest's page.

Plane of Sky has its own tracker: every class's Test quests with have / need chips per item, item stats on hover, and sorting by closest to done.

Loot, upgrades and farming

  1. Fill in your gear under the Build tab, or let the Gear tab read it. That profile is what upgrades are measured against.
  2. Open Zone Loot, pick a zone, and see every mob the wiki lists there and what each drops, beside how many you have looted yourself and your drops per hour. Drops that beat what you wear carry an upgrade chip; there is a switch to show upgrades only.
  3. The Build tab lists where to farm your upgrades, zone by zone, with the mobs that drop them.
  4. Wish-list an item from its page and you get an alert and a card when it drops for you, and when you enter a zone where it drops. Your own loot only: the log has no line for what other players loot.
  5. The Crafting tab shows what you can make from what you hold, what you are one ingredient away from, and every recipe with what you are missing.

Sharing your setup

Your whole settings bundle exports as one string or a file: alerts, volume, overlay look, view preferences, favourites. It carries no file paths, no window positions and no character progress, so it is safe to hand to a guildmate. Importing it on another PC adds to what is there rather than replacing it.

Coming from EQ Legends Companion? Nothing to do. EQ Zera reads the same settings folder, so alerts, sound packs, overlay positions and character history are there on first launch.

Updates and versions

EQ Zera checks GitHub shortly after launch and every few hours after that. When a new build is out you get a card on the celebration overlay, a chip in the nav, and a line in Preferences → Updates. Click once to download, again to restart into it. Nothing downloads until you click; a downloaded build is applied the next time you close the app. Every download is verified against the SHA-512 in the release feed.

The What's new panel lists what changed in each release, including the ones you skipped. Preferences shows the version you are running; quote it in a bug report.

Troubleshooting

Nothing shows up

Check that logging is on (/log on in game, once per character) and that the log folder in Preferences is the one the game writes to. A character that has never logged has no file to read.

Overlays are not visible over the game

The game is in exclusive fullscreen. Switch to borderless windowed in the game's display options.

Fights end after one second, or timers are wrong

Fixed in 1.17.0: the engine could not learn your time zone on some machines and read every line as hours old. Update, and the performance panel shows which clock the engine is on.

SmartScreen blocks the installer

Releases since 1.20.1 are code signed and the prompt names the publisher, Jack Thomas. If SmartScreen still warns while the certificate is new, click More info, then Run anyway. The download is verified against its hash before installing.

The update card never appears

The check runs about 45 seconds after launch and then every four hours. Preferences → Updates has a manual check and shows the current state.

Something else

Send feedback from inside the app with a log slice, or write in.

What it does Install Guides Screens Support FAQ Contact GitHub

A desktop toolkit for EverQuest Legends

EQ Zera

The live DPS meter, floating overlays and quest tracker for EverQuest Legends.

It reads the log the game already writes. Nothing touches the game.

Download for Windows All releases

v1.22.1Windows 10 / 11, 64-bit134 MBFree, open sourceUpdates itself

Reads your log only

Nothing is injected into EverQuest, no game files are touched, no memory is read, nothing is automated. Type /log on and it has something to show.

Nothing leaves your PC

No telemetry endpoint is compiled in. The only network calls are the ones you can see: the EQ Legends wiki for item and mob data, and GitHub for updates.

Open source

The whole app, including the Rust log engine, is on GitHub under the Functional Source License. Read it, build it, file an issue.

What it does

A DPS meter, overlays, quest and loot tracking for EverQuest Legends

EQ Zera watches the log file EverQuest Legends writes and turns every line into something you can act on while you play. Per character, per fight, per zone.

Live from the log, over the game

Every number on this page comes from one source: the plain-text log EverQuest Legends writes. Nothing reads the game, so nothing can break when the game patches; if the log says it, EQ Zera shows it.

Live DPS meter

Per-fight and per-zone damage and healing numbers with fight history. Click a fight to see every hit, miss and resist that made the number, drill into each attack and spell, and scrub a timeline of the pull. Charm pets are counted correctly.

Floating overlays

Small always-on-top meters you leave over the game: damage or healing, scoped to the current fight or the whole zone, plus a farm meter with kills, XP, drops and coin per hour. Lock one and it becomes click-through.

Quest tracker and quest item pop-ups

Track any EverQuest Legends quest from its page and follow its steps as a checklist. Looting an item lights its step, hailing the NPC ticks the hail, and a turn-in completes it with a card and your alert. Loot something a quest needs and a pop-up names the quest and where it starts.

Plane of Sky tracker

Every class's Plane of Sky Test quests with have / need chips per item, item stats on hover, and sorting by closest to done.

Loot, upgrades and where to farm

A running history of what you looted and what each item is for. Zone Loot shows every mob the wiki lists in a zone and what it drops, with an upgrade chip when a drop beats what you wear, and the Build tab lists where to farm your upgrades, zone by zone.

Crafting and wish lists

What you can make from what you hold, what you are one ingredient away from, and every recipe with what you are missing. Wish-list an item and get an alert when it drops or when you enter a zone where it does.

Your character, in 3D

A model of your character with race, sex and face controls for the classic races and Iksar. Preview any wearable item on it from the Gear tab or an item page, one click back to your real gear.

Alerts, timers and recaps

Sound alerts for a charm break, a fading buff, a raid target dying, or any log line you write a rule for. Buff and debuff timers, XP and AA progress, raid-target history, and a death recap that says who killed you and what hit you in the last fifteen seconds.

The app

Every tab, from a real session

Captured on 2026-09-08 from a level 50 monk's log. Click any screen to open it full size.

Install

Install EQ Zera on Windows in a minute

A one-click, per-user install like Discord. No admin prompt, no wizard. It adds a Start menu and desktop shortcut.

Download the installer

eq-zera-Setup.exe is always the newest build. Requires 64-bit Windows 10 or 11.

Run the installer

The installer is code signed, so the Windows prompt names the publisher, Jack Thomas. If SmartScreen still shows “Windows protected your PC” while the new certificate earns its reputation, click More info, then Run anyway.

Turn on logging in game

In EverQuest Legends type /log on. The app finds your log folder on its own, usually under Daybreak Game Company, Installed Games, EverQuest Legends, Logs.

Play

Fight something and the meter fills in. Overlays sit over the game in windowed or borderless mode; exclusive fullscreen cannot be overlaid by anything.

Coming from EQ Legends Companion?

EQ Zera continues where the EverQuest Companion app stopped

The same app, still maintained

EQ Legends Companion (the everquest-companion project by Josh Moyers) ended development in September 2026. EQ Zera is its continuation: the same DPS meter, overlays, Plane of Sky tracker, loot history and alerts, with new releases, a self-updater that works, and an open issue tracker.

Everything added since the fork is listed under What's new: the quest tracker, quest item pop-ups, Zone Loot, upgrade finder, crafting, wish lists, the farm meter, death recap and the 3D character model.

Switching takes one install

EQ Zera reads the same settings folder, so your alerts, sound packs, overlay positions and character history carry over on first launch. Nothing is moved or deleted; the old install keeps working if you leave it.

Looking for the EQ Legends Companion download? The original project no longer publishes builds. The EQ Zera installer is the current one.

Updates and trust

It updates itself, and it tells you the terms

How updates work

An installed copy checks GitHub shortly after launch and every few hours after that. When a newer build is out you get a card on the celebration overlay and a note in Preferences. Nothing downloads until you click, and a downloaded build is applied the next time you close the app.

Every download is verified against the SHA-512 in the release feed, so a corrupted or substituted file fails to install.

What is and is not verified

Since 1.20.1 every release carries an Authenticode signature issued through Azure Trusted Signing, with Jack Thomas as the publisher. The app refuses any update that is not signed by that publisher, so both the download and its author are verified. Right-click the installer and open Digital Signatures to check it yourself; the full statement is in the repository's SECURITY.md.

EQ Zera carries the upstream license: free to use, modify and share for non-commercial purposes, converting to MIT on the license's schedule.

FAQ

Questions people ask before installing

Is a log parser allowed in EverQuest Legends?

EQ Zera reads the plain-text log file the game writes when you type /log on. It does not read game memory, inject anything, send input, or automate play. Log parsers of this kind have been part of EverQuest for over twenty years.

Is EQ Zera free?

Yes. It is open source under the Functional Source License and there is nothing to buy, no account and no sign-in.

Does it work on Mac or Linux?

The installer is Windows 10 and 11 only. Players have run it under Wine and CrossOver; the engine now learns your time zone so timers are right there too, but it is not a supported platform.

Is the installer signed?

Yes. Releases since 1.20.1 are code signed through Azure Trusted Signing and the Windows prompt names the publisher. If SmartScreen still warns while the certificate is new, click More info, then Run anyway. The download is also verified against a SHA-512 hash before it installs.

Do the overlays work in fullscreen?

In windowed and borderless windowed mode, yes. Exclusive fullscreen cannot be overlaid by any program, so switch to borderless if you want meters over the game.

Where do the item, mob and quest data come from?

From the EQ Legends wiki, fetched on demand and cached. Quest steps for the tracker are built from the wiki's walkthrough pages.

Does it send my data anywhere?

No. No telemetry endpoint is compiled in. Feedback goes out only when you choose to send it, through your own mail app or a GitHub issue, and you see the report first.

How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?

Open a GitHub issue, or use Send feedback inside the app, which fills the report in for you.

Support

Buy the author a coffee

EQ Zera is free and stays free. It is built and maintained by one player in the evenings, and the site, the domain and the code-signing certificate cost real money. If it has saved you a wipe or found you an upgrade, a coffee is a fine way to say so.

Donations buy nothing extra: no features are locked, no ads appear, and the app never asks.

Buy me a coffee on Venmo

Venmo @eqzera is the project's business profile, not a personal account. Venmo is US-only; if you are elsewhere, a kind word in the contact form is just as welcome.
